```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(tidypopgen)
library(ggplot2)
```

```{r set-directories}
res_dir <- "../results/s03_malagasy_pca/"
```

# Load gt

```{r}
malagasy_merged <-
  gt_load("../data/intermediate/rbind_data/malagasy_merge_clean_ld.gt")
```

This script creates a PCA of only Malagasy individuals, using the
Malagasy dataset, comprising of `r nrow(malagasy_merged)` individuals
and `r ncol(malagasy_merged)` loci.

```{r}
count_loci(malagasy_merged)
nrow(malagasy_merged)
```

# Count individuals from each group 

```{r}
pierron_data <- length(which(malagasy_merged$population %in% c("Mikea", "Vezo", "Temoro")))
pierron_data
nrow(malagasy_merged) - pierron_data
```

# Set imputed

```{r}
gt_set_imputed(malagasy_merged, TRUE)
```

# PCA

```{r}
random_pca <- gt_pca_randomSVD(malagasy_merged, total_var = TRUE)
pcs <- as.data.frame(random_pca$u)
variance <- tidy(random_pca)
```

# Digeo Individuals

```{r}
malagasy_sample_sheet <-
  as_tibble(read.csv("../data/raw/data_input/Malagasy_pop_gen_sample_sheet_2015_cleaned.csv"))
diego_groups <- malagasy_sample_sheet %>% filter(District == "Diego")
diego <- malagasy_merged %>%
  filter(sub("RR.*", "", id) %in% diego_groups$Sample.ID)
diego$ethnicity <- diego_groups$Ethnic.group[match(sub("RR.*", "", diego$id), diego_groups$Sample.ID)]
unique(diego$ethnicity)
```

# Plot

```{r}
malagasy_merged[malagasy_merged$population == "Sakalava_Tsimihety", "population"] <- "Sakalava/Tsimihety"
malagasy_merged[malagasy_merged$population == "Diego", "population"] <- "Diego Mixed"

ggplot(pcs, aes(
  x = V1, y = V2,
  group = malagasy_merged$population,
  colour = malagasy_merged$population,
  shape = malagasy_merged$population,
  fill = malagasy_merged$population
)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 1) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(1, 3, 7, 15, 17, 19, 21, 23)) +
  labs(
    title = NULL,
    x = paste0("PC 1 (", round(variance$percent[1], 2), "%)"),
    y = paste0("PC 2 (", round(variance$percent[2], 2), "%)"),
    colour = NULL, shape = NULL, fill = NULL
  ) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.line = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
    legend.position = c(0.3, 0.3)
  )

ggsave(paste0(res_dir, "madagascar_pca.jpg"), width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 300)
```

```{r}
autoplot(random_pca, type = "scree")
```

This PCA uses the KING relatedness filtering of 0.088, equivalent to
second degree relatives. There is justification for keeping second
degree close relatives (aunts, uncles, grandparents, grandchildren,
nieces, nephews, and half-siblings) because the prevalence of
consanguinity in each population is unknown, but likely to be high in
places, and therefore removing all second degree relatives may
substantially reduce the sample size.

However, altering the relatedness filtering only reduced the sample size
by \~10. The PCA plot shows a similar distribution of the Malagasy
samples, but with a slightly different spread and slightly reduced
explained variance when compared to relatedness filtering with a kinship
coefficient of 0.177 (first degree relatives). It therefore appears that
the relatedness filtering has a small effect on the PCA, but the overall
structure of the Malagasy samples is maintained.

'the KING option ‘‘–unrelated’’ proceeds as follows. Related individuals
(defined by existing pedigree or estimated kinship coefficient ,0.088)
are first clustered into connected groups (i.e., families). Within each
family cluster, individuals are ranked according to the count of
unrelated family members (having estimated kinship coefficient ,0.022).
To construct a set of unrelated individuals, we first select the
individual with the largest count of unrelated individuals within the
family cluster. We then proceed to choose the individual with the next
highest rank (number of unrelated family members) within the family
cluster, only if that individual is not related to any of the previously
selected individuals in the list of unrelated individuals' Manichaikul
et al., 2010)

'--related --degree 2 specifies that only related pairs (up to the
2nd-degree in this case) between families are included in the output.
Specifically all pairs across families with a kinship coefficient less
than 0.0884 will be excluded from the output. '

## Recording R environment

Part of ensuring our workflow is reproducible is to keep track of the R
environment. We will automatically save our R environment into a file
called `r_environment.json`.

```{r save-r-environment, echo=FALSE, results='hide', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE, results='hide', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
filename_rmd <- "s03_malagasy_pca.Rmd"
filename_renv <- paste0(
  res_dir, "/renv_",
  tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(filename_rmd)),
  ".json"
)
renv::lockfile_write(renv::lockfile_create(), file = filename_renv)
xfun::session_info()
```
